correctness.rationale: With columns as senders, the arrival mass is the unique solution u=1+Q(I−D)u, because the induced column norm is less than one. For a target w set u=D⁻¹w; the induced edge flow must have receiver demands r_i=u_i−1 and sender supplies c_j=(1−τ_j)u_j. The total margin difference is Σw_i−n. If w satisfies the stated normalization and lower bounds then r_i≥0 and c_j>0. In the bipartite construction, a cut crossing an allowed internal arc already costs at least C=Σc_j; otherwise, if S denotes receivers on the sink side, all their neighboring senders must also lie there. The cut costs at least c(Γ⁻(S))+r(V∖S)≥C, with that lower bound attained by the minimal sender choice for each S. A C-flow thus exists and division by the positive c_j gives exactly the required stochastic columns and target resolvent, including exact rational witnesses by scaling capacities to integers. A missing outgoing arc at a sender violates the S=V cut. On a complete loopless graph every cut with |S|≥2 is automatic, yielding precisely the box intersected with the normalized hyperplane; singleton cuts give w_i−τ≤(1−τ)(n−w_i). When every other vertex sends only to the hub this inequality is an equality, whatever admissible split the hub uses; the recorded equal split is a valid witness. The bound equals n/2 only at n=2 for τ>0 and tends to n/2 as τ decreases to zero. The disconnected-triangle example has all singleton inequalities, but violates the first component cut by 18/5−33/10=3/10.
residual_risks: The frozen rational test count corroborates implementation only. The unrestricted result follows from the exact cut proof. No assertion of uniqueness of the hub's equal split is made.

originality.rationale: The strongest inspected comparison, Berend's inverse PageRank, asks a mathematically equivalent common-retention target question when teleportation is uniform, but its stated exact case uses full support with self-transitions and its sparse discussion provides limited obstructions rather than the exact cuts. The frozen result's supported distinct content is the explicit cut characterization and construction for fixed heterogeneous retention on a fixed graph, and the sharp complete-loopless attainable polytope as a consequence. The underlying max-flow criterion itself is classical, and this is not a claim to have originated prescribed PageRank or flow-based delegation.
residual_risks: A matching exact support-constrained stationary-design theorem under another name remains possible; priority is bounded by the actual inspected statements.
The equivalence to common-retention PageRank removes novelty from the problem formulation itself.

checked_sources: Berend §5.3 for motivation of exact targets and sparse obstructions
value.rationale: An inverse target on a fixed trust graph is a natural design and obstruction question. The exact polytope replaces an apparent nonlinear inverse problem by one flow test that gives either a realizable delegation or a concrete obstructing group. The disconnected example makes the collective limitation real, and the sharp complete-network box quantifies the loss of concentration caused by forbidding self-arcs. The general solution and its witnesses, rather than the short cap derivation in isolation, justify the value.
residual_risks: No prediction of strategic choice or pivotal voting power follows, and positivity on all permitted arcs is not required by this model.
